title: LFM3: dense hybrid of gated short-conv, full and sliding (256) layers, sandwich norms, headwise scalar gate

findings.workload: tslab ab: protocol long-synthesis (2,918 prompt tokens), 128 decode, chunk off; off against gqa:attn_decode_kernel=gqa; 3 clean pairs, 4 of 12 runs dirty (other sessions' rustc)
findings.conditions: swap 27.5 GB used but 85% memory free (stale swap); null record 1793218364008-64718-24 in the same experiment
findings.note: a 3-round tslab profile the same day (lfm3-a1-profile, mostly dirty) read the same direction: decode digests identical between arms on short-explanation and long-synthesis, prefill logits digests differ (KL-bounded kernel), short-prompt decode +3%

findings.workload: tslab ab after the flip: protocol long-synthesis (2,918 prompt tokens), 128 decode, chunk off, --metric decode_tok_s; default (GQA) against barrier:attn_decode_kernel=barrier; 3 clean pairs, 0 dirty
findings.conditions: null record 1793229818920-71333-16 in the same experiment; swap about 24 GB used (stale); every default run printed [engaged] attn_decode_gqa with no env set, every barrier run attn_decode_barrier
findings.note: the candidate is the old kernel, so a loss confirms the default. An earlier run of the same pair without --metric (experiment lfm3-b2-gqa-default, verdict 1793228595096-11051-16) measured prefill_tok_s, the per-token step under chunk off: -10.71%, CI [-14.28%, -10.24%]. Both quality rows re-froze by the playbook protocol the same day (docs/LFM3_PHASE0.md, Decode attention): greedy digests unchanged, perplexity 14.7455 -> 14.7434 and 15.8615 -> 15.8614

findings.workload: tslab kernel --bench attn_decode,int4_matmul,qkv_concurrent at the install's shapes
findings.conditions: in-process benches, primed int4_matmul; attn_decode and qkv_concurrent do not prime yet
findings.note: decode is mostly GEMV time (about 3.5 of 4.6 ms per token); mma8 at one row is 1.19-1.57x a GEMV, so it is not a decode lever here; Steel at 512 rows costs 0.045-0.098x the per-row GEMV

findings.workload: tslab kernel --bench ane_matmul, programs from gen_ane_sweep_programs.py at 512x2048, 2048x2048, 2048x7680, 6144x2048, 7680x2048 and 128-2048 tokens, shares 1.0, 0.7, 0.5, 0.3
findings.conditions: wall per matmul with conversions and host handoff; energy is IOReport modeled whole machine, not wall power
findings.note: speed: neither the ANE nor any split beats Steel at any point (512x2048 crosses only above about 2,600 tokens). Energy gate routes most points to the ANE at about 0.4-0.55x Steel's modeled joules: an energy mode, not a speed one, and it needs a chunked prefill first

findings.workload: tslab profile: short-explanation (57 tokens) and long-synthesis (2,918), 128 decode, chunk off, 2 rounds per arm, 0 dirty; llama-bench (Homebrew llama.cpp build 11960) on the same Q8_0 GGUF: pp512, pp2048, tg128, 3 reps
findings.conditions: the llama.cpp numbers are from its own harness, not a tslab ledger; tg128 starts from an empty context
findings.note: decode 0.63x llama.cpp (about 180 against 280 GB/s), prefill about 32x behind because ours is sequential

findings.workload: tslab ab: protocol long-synthesis (2,918 prompt tokens), 32 decode, chunk 128; seq:lfm3_chunked_prefill=0 against the default driver; 3 clean pairs
findings.conditions: null record 1793221115774-6208-16 in the same experiment; a three-arm profile the same day (lfm3-c1-chunk, 2 rounds, 0 dirty) read 12.95-12.99 s seq, 4.49-4.61 s exact, 1.47-1.48 s default for the 2,918-token prompt, with the exact arm's prefill logits digest equal to seq's and all three arms' 128-token greedy decode digests equal
findings.note: measured before main's TURBOSPARK_PREFILL_SMALL_N route existed; it now engages on the default arm for narrow projections, unmeasured for speed here

findings.workload: crates/bench/tests/lfm3_prefill_arm_probe.rs: docs corpus slices of 64-3000 tokens in 128-token chunks; reference is the exact arm, re-checked bit-identical to sequential produce at 64 and 200 tokens
findings.note: comparable to Qwen3.8's Steel arm (1.5e-5). Re-run after the GQA decode default: 1.89e-5 / 1.72e-5; on top of main's prefill_small_n route: 2.19e-5 / 1.41e-5, top-1 6/6

open_questions: ANE split for the chunked prefill: the matmul bench says no speed win at these shapes (lfm3.ane-matmul-2026-10-28), only modeled energy; an energy-mode arm would be the only reason to wire it
a concurrent q/k/v(+gate) encoder: the triple costs 0.611x serial in the kernel bench, about 0.24 ms per token over 11 attention layers if it carries over
the q8_0 decode GEMV reads about 180 GB/s against llama.cpp's about 280 on the same bytes; no lab bench times dtype 6
the bimodal short-explanation decode in docs/LFM3_PHASE0.md did not reproduce in 26 tslab runs on 2026-10-28
traps: the GGUF Q8_0 install has no batched GEMM: its prefill is sequential, use --chunk off
phase buckets are final_only: the whole layer stack is one command buffer, so profile shows about 95% final wait; use kernel benches or trace for shares
installs live in ~/models (lfm3-1.7b-mlx-4bit, lfm3-1.7b-q8), not the catalog store
